question: do the 13 Expert Advisors of github.com/geraked/metatrader5 (MIT) carry an edge in their entry signal, beyond walks matched to each series, and is the author's grid-without-stops profit anything more than the grid's shape, which a random walk also shows until it blows up
source: the repo's Experts/*.mq5, Indicators/*.mq5 and Include/EAUtils.mqh, Cot.mqh, ported to Python in research/ideas/geraked_ind.py (indicators) and geraked_eas.py (signals), geraked_sim.py (trade, grid and account engines); every default input kept
timing: every EA reads the last closed bar on the first tick of a new bar: the signal is computed on bar t's close and fills at bar t+1's open. Inputs that read the forming bar (Ask in 2MAAOS and NWERSIASF, a SL_SWING with start 0, DHLAOS's j = 0 scan, 3MAF's fractal at buffer 2) see only bar t+1's open. 2MAAOS and NWERSIASF poll on a timer within the bar; here they are checked at the open only
path: inside a bar price runs open -> low -> high -> close on an up bar and open -> high -> low -> close on a down bar; stops, targets, trails and grid levels are checked at those four vertices (exact for that path); a level crossed by a gap fills at the open

mode_S.role: PRIMARY - the entry signal with its own coded exits
mode_S.settings: IgnoreSL = IgnoreTP = false, Grid = false, the EA's own Reverse, Trail and TrailingStopLevel (50% of the coded stop distance, from breakeven on), CloseOrders/CloseOnProfit and MinPosInterval as coded; one position at a time per series
mode_S.R: the coded stop distance at the fill (|entry - SL|); R net of cost; any stop fill takes 0.05 ATR(14) of adverse slippage
mode_S.reverse: the EA's own Reverse semantics: the opposite side with SL at the coded TP and TP at the coded SL; where an EA codes no TP (CEZLSMA) the stop is mirrored at the same distance
mode_S.tail: P(N R) for N in 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 10 = share of entries whose price reaches +N R before the coded initial stop (first passage, before costs, exits ignored, to the end of data); on a martingale it is 1/(N+1)

mode_G.role: the author's defaults: the account in money with the grid as coded
mode_G.settings: each EA's default inputs (IgnoreSL/IgnoreTP, Grid, GridVolMult, GridMaxLvl, GridTrailingStopLevel, Trail, Reverse, CloseOrders); risk 1% (RISK_DEFAULT: min(balance, free margin) x 1% / coded stop distance, the lot grid of the broker's spec); the author's own Risk is also run on the author's own cells
mode_G.account: 10,000 USD, leverage 1:100 on every instrument, margin = lots x contract value at the fill / 100; no new order when free margin is short (NO_MONEY); stop-out at 50% margin level closes the whole grid; spread paid on every fill, no swap or commission
mode_G.measures: CAGR, max drawdown of equity at bar closes, worst open-equity drawdown (equity at each adverse vertex against its running peak), days to the first stop-out, ruin (equity at or below 10% of the start: trading stops), share of grid cycles that reach GridMaxLvl
mode_G.walks: the identical engine on the same matched walks as Mode S (price level matched: walks are geometric from the real first price), same spec, same cost in ATR units

mode_R.role: the risk-management layer (EAUtils.mqh / EATemplate*.mq5), one factor at a time on each EA's Mode S signals
mode_R.base: Mode S (coded stop, coded TP, the EA's trail), RISK_DEFAULT 1%, no martingale, no equity limit, no spread limit, one position

factors.stop: SL_SWING, SL_AR, SL_MR, SL_FIXED_POINT with the EA's SLLookback/SLDev (10 / 60 points where it has none), TP = TPCoef x the new distance
factors.sizing: RISK_DEFAULT 1%, RISK_EQUITY 1%, FIXED_VOL (the lots the first trade gets at 1%, fixed), MIN_AMOUNT (one lot step per equity / Risk, Risk set so the first trade matches)
factors.martingale: on, martingaleRisk 4% (after a losing deal: 2 x the last loss / the new TP distance, capped at 4% of balance)
factors.equity_limit: EquityDrawdownLimit 5% (no grid), and 20% with the author's grid
factors.spread_limit: skip a signal whose bar spread exceeds 2x the series' median bar spread (MT5 only)
factors.grid: the author's grid with stops ignored, risk 1% (= Mode G) as the reference line
factors.news: skipped: the lab holds no economic calendar
factors.knn: Knn.mqh is used by no EA: not tested

mode_R.measures: mean R a trade and P(N R) against 1/(N+1); account CAGR, max drawdown, worst open-equity drawdown; Monte Carlo ruin from 2,000 resampled 1,000-trade sequences (P(touching -50%), P(ending below the start)); real and both walks
mode_R.expectation: on a martingale no stop, trail, sizing or martingale scheme creates expectancy (E[net] = -(c/2) x turnover): on the walks every factor should keep mean R at minus costs while drawdown and ruin move; on real data a factor that moves R beyond what the walks show is reported as an interaction with something real

COT1.data: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures, futures only (fut_fin_txt), Dealer (primary class) and Leveraged Funds (secondary), fetched from cftc.gov; the 8 currency contracts the EA lists
COT1.lag: the EA's own window: on Monday/Tuesday it reads the report dated Monday-Wednesday of the previous week (Tuesday's positions, released Friday); entries from Monday 00:00 UTC (03:00 server time), checked every 15 minutes Monday and Tuesday
COT1.signals: per class: of the latest report, the two currencies with a positive net change and the highest long share against the two with a negative net change and the highest short share; their pairs that exist at this broker (buy green/red, or sell red/green); one position at a time across symbols, one deal a symbol a week
COT1.bars: managed on 15m bars of the 12 FX pairs; its walks are matched walks of those pairs carrying the same signals

data.mt5: the broker's bars (mt5bt.db) for every symbol in run.FAMILY: fx 12, metal 5, index 7, energy 2, crypto_cfd 35, deriv 15; 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d
data.stock: the broker's stock CFD bars on the lab (seqlab, 1h and 1d only): 50 tickers drawn once with numpy seed 7 from the .N/.OQ files
data.author_cells: each EA's Test/ symbol and timeframe where the broker has it: 2MAAOS EURUSD+USDCAD 4h; 2MACDSTO NZDUSD 3h (resampled from 1h); 3MACD AUDUSD 5m; 3MAF USDCAD 15m; BBRSI XAUUSD 5m; CEZLSMA AUDUSD 15m; DHLAOS AUDUSD 5m; NWERSIASF USDCAD+AUDUSD 2h (resampled from 1h); COT1 FX daily (as above). Not available: EURCAD, EURCHF, NZDCAD (AFAOSMD 30m), AUDCAD (LRCUTB). 2MOMEMA and LRCMACD have no Test folder. The broker's 5m history is about six months

classes.report: every result per asset class and pooled: fx, metal, index, energy, crypto_cfd, binance, stock, deriv_diffusive (Volatility 10/25/50/75/100, Step, Step 200, Step 500, Drift Switch 10/20/30), deriv_jumpy (Boom 1000, Crash 1000, Jump 50), and Range Break 100 on its own line
classes.pooled: MT5 non-Deriv = fx + metal + index + energy + crypto_cfd; Deriv never pooled with it

costs: MT5: the broker's spread floor (run.spread_floor); where it is zero (crypto CFDs, XPT, XPD, XCU) the series' median bar spread, frozen; a series whose cost exceeds 0.5 x its median ATR(14) is dropped and listed. Binance 0.07% of price a trade. Stocks: the bars carry no spread, so 0.05% of price a trade, frozen. Stop fills 0.05 ATR(14) of slippage. Walks pay the real series' cost in ATR units at the same bar

controls.iid: a Gaussian walk in log price matched to the series' sigma, 256 sub-steps a bar, the real timestamps, starting at the real first price
controls.garch: GARCH(1,1) (alpha 0.08, beta 0.9) with the same sigma, otherwise the same
controls.coin: the EA's real fills with a random side, the same stop distance, TP multiple, trail and close rule

primary: per EA: Mode S, MT5 non-Deriv pooled, 15m-1d pooled (COT1: its FX pairs on 15m)
passes_if: mean R > 0 after costs with the day-bootstrap 90% interval above 0; mean R > 0 before and after 2024-01-01; above the iid walk, the GARCH walk and the coin twin on the same cell; and Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.10 across the 13 EAs on the one-sided day-bootstrap p
secondary: every EA x asset class x timeframe cell of Mode S, BH at q = 0.10 across all of them (the count is reported); author cells; Mode G and Mode R are descriptive
amended_after_first_run: 2026-10-04, after the first full run and before the results were written up: an order whose stop sits inside the broker's stops level is refused, as the broker refuses it (TRADE_RETCODE_INVALID_STOPS): MT5 symbols use their spec's stops level (at least 10 points), Binance and stocks 1 bp of price. The first run let a stop a point or two from the fill through, and cost / a near-zero risk made a few hundred trades' R explode (to -10^8 on one Deriv cell), contaminating means and the Monte Carlo ruin. Everything was re-run with the refusal in the engine (2.4% of entries); the first run's primary verdicts were the same (no EA passes)
